competitive_landscape: Today: the diesel Robben Island ferry and conventional peninsula tour boats. The pain is weather exposure and an ageing tour fleet — the status quo a cleaner, smoother tier improves on.

demand_signals.label: African gateway
demand_signals.note: Establishes Navier presence on the African coast

journeys.with_navier: A foiling run around the peninsula

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Table Bay and False Bay corridors (Robben Island ~7 nm, Hout Bay ~12 nm, False Bay ~22–30 nm) sit inside the all-electric envelope; routing flexes around the Cape's wind as existing operators already do.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Held in reserve for longer exposed-coast corridors where all-weather range matters.

precedents.what: A foiling-electric vessel network at national scale (~100 vessels / $100M, 3-year phasing)
precedents.why_it_matters: Proves foiling-electric works as an at-scale transfer-and-island-hopping network, not just a pilot.

regulatory_note: South African maritime and tourism authorities license the Robben Island and peninsula routes; growing focus on the Cape's marine-protected areas favours zero-emission, low-wake operation.
seasonality: The Cape is famously windy (the 'Cape Doctor' SE wind in summer); routing and scheduling flex around wind windows, with sheltered Table Bay running most reliably.
summary: Cape Town wraps around Table Bay with the V&A Waterfront among the continent's most-visited destinations, a constant Robben Island heritage ferry, and a dramatic peninsula tourism coast. It establishes Navier's African presence as a global tourism flagship.

use_cases.body: A faster, smoother, zero-emission Robben Island crossing (~7 nm).
